summary.text: John Mannion is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent in New York's 22nd District, seeking a second term. A former high school science teacher and teachers' union president, he served in the New York State Senate from 2020 to 2024 before winning the House seat in 2024. He sits on the House Agriculture and Education and Workforce committees.

paragraphs.text: Mannion was born in Syracuse, New York, in 1968. His official biography says he was raised on Syracuse's Tipperary Hill and is the grandson of Irish immigrants.
He earned a bachelor's degree in biology from Binghamton University and a master's degree in secondary education from SUNY Oswego.

Mannion spent nearly 30 years teaching high school science, including Advanced Placement Biology and Chemistry, according to his official biography. He also served eight years as president of the West Genesee Teachers' Association, which the biography says represented about 400 teachers, school nurses and school psychologists.
He lost the 2018 race for the 50th State Senate District to Republican Bob Antonacci, then won the seat in 2020 over Republican Angi Renna.

In the Senate, where he served from 2020 to 2024, Mannion narrowly won re-election in 2022 after a recount and was the founding chair of the Committee on Disabilities. His official biography says he helped enact New York's Green CHIPS legislation and, as a state senator, secured four consecutive cost-of-living increases for Direct Support Professionals.

Mannion won the 2024 Democratic primary and then the general election against Republican incumbent Brandon Williams, and he took office in January 2025. The district covers Central New York and the Mohawk Valley, including Syracuse and Utica.

In the House he serves on the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on Agriculture. His first bill was the Protecting Students with Disabilities Act, and he introduced the Science of Reading Act, which passed the House.
Mannion lives in Geddes with his wife, Jennifer, an elementary school teacher; they have three children, according to his official biography.
